core_claim: Steinberg Chromaspheres converts imported audio samples into playable sounds using four synthesis engines and thirty sound-shaping modes.
topic: Steinberg's free Chromaspheres instrument for HALion Sonic and HALion, which converts imported samples into playable sounds through wavetable, granular, spectral and sample-based engines.
title: One Sample, Thirty Sound Modes: Steinberg Chromaspheres
hook: What if one recording could become a completely different playable instrument?
description: A global music-technology explainer about Steinberg Chromaspheres, a free HALion Sonic instrument. Production Expert and Synth News independently describe its sample-to-playable-instrument workflow, four synthesis engines and thirty sound-shaping modes. The video uses only conceptual diagrams and an original/CC0 violin phrase as an illustration. It is not a hands-on Violin Prince test: do not claim the sample was processed through Chromaspheres, show a fabricated plugin interface, or invent a before-and-after result.
cover_payoff: Use a disclosed original or CC0 violin sample as the source in a conceptual diagram showing how one recording can become a playable instrument. Do not claim the sample was processed in Chromaspheres or fake a software demonstration; keep the audible phrase original and clearly illustrative.
narration_script: Can one recording become a playable instrument? Steinberg’s free Chromaspheres instrument turns samples into sounds. One engine can turn a sample into thirty prepared sound modes. Composers can create new source material from their recordings.

narration_evidence.quote: turns any sample dropped onto it into a playable sound
The idea fits in one sentence: drop an audio file into the instrument, pick an engine, then one of the 30 sound modes Steinberg has prepared.
aimed at composers and sound designers who want to build new source material from their own recordings
